_note: Shown by the menu's Resources and sources button (scripts/ui/sources.gd). Keep it honest: say what is real, what is rounded, and what is invented for gameplay. Every url was checked (HTTP 200) on 14 Nov 2026; check again before the final submission. The missions' own sources are in each level file's based_on block and are listed automatically.
accuracy: Real physics: one low Earth orbit at about 550 km takes about 95 minutes, and the Earth hides the Sun for up to about 35 of them. That is why every satellite needs a battery.
Real rules: CubeSats come in standard sizes (1U is a 10 cm cube, 3U is three of them), and a rideshare rocket sells a slot with a hard mass limit.
Real process: build, test, licence and ship really do run in that order, and radio and imaging licences can take months.
Real launch stages: max-Q, the second-stage burn and separation are the moments a real launch is most likely to go wrong.
Rounded: part masses, power and data rates are in the right range for CubeSat parts, but rounded so the maths is easy.
Invented for gameplay: prices, the exact risk rules, fuel use and the event cards. They teach the trade-off, not the exact number.
Every screen with made-up numbers says PLACEHOLDER NUMBERS in the bottom bar.
